text:
maya: Heads up — infra CI for gpu-provisioner keep failing on master. GHA job `provision` times out after 30m on runs triggered by PRs that touch cluster config + autoscaler. Anyone else seeing this?

ci-bot: Workflow run failed: redwood/infra/gpu-provisioner #342 by @jordan — Job `provision` timed out (30m). :x:

samir: Yep, saw it. The terraform apply seems to hang waiting on instance create then finally errors with a 409. Log snippet: 
```
googleapi: Error 409: The resource 'projects/redwood/zones/us-west1-b/instances/gpu-node-001' already exists, alreadyExists
```

jasper: Also seeing flaky `actions/cache` restores before that — sometimes restoration takes 5-8m then fails with 502/504 from storage.googleapis.com. When cache fails, the job repeats expensive operations and extends runtime.

li: I think it's a concurrency + state locking problem. We still use GCS backend with state locks, but if two runs run plan/apply close together the race still happens (ours isn't using isolated TF workspaces per PR).

samir: We have `concurrency:` in a few repos but it's keyed off `${{ github.ref }}` which is different for PRs vs branches. So two PR runs can still overlap.

maya: Minimal repro command from CI: 
```bash
# runs inside gha job
terraform init -backend-config=\"bucket=redwood-terraform-state\"
terraform plan -var-file=pr-123.tfvars
terraform apply -auto-approve -var-file=pr-123.tfvars
# apply hits lock wait then eventually times out/409
```

jasper: Another angle — GCP API quota for GPUs is hitting high utilization in us-west1 this morning. If quota is low, create calls can be retried for a long time and then return conflicts. I saw similar in the cloud console.

sre-oncall: Confirmed: GPU quota at 88% in us-west1, many failed create calls during 09:04-09:22 UTC. I can temporarily raise alerting thresholds and file a quota request, but that takes time.

li: Short-term mitigation options: 1) stop running provision on PRs (only run on main / manual), 2) enforce a repo-level concurrency group that serializes provision jobs, 3) add stronger cache retry/backoff and reduce cache churn.

maya: I'm going to open a PR to disable automatic `apply` on PR workflows and add a `workflow_dispatch`/manual gate. Will also add notice in PR template.

samir: I'll draft a follow-up PR to add `concurrency:
  group: infra-provision-serialize
  cancel-in-progress: false` so these always run one at a time across refs. Also add `terraform apply -lock-timeout=600s` and a retry wrapper for cache restore: 
```yaml
- name: Restore cache
  uses: actions/cache@v3
  with:
    path: .terraform
    key: ${{ runner.os }}-tf-${{ hashFiles('**/*.tf') }}
  continue-on-error: true
- name: Cache sanity wait
  run: |
    for i in {1..5}; do sleep $((i*5)); test -d .terraform && break; done
```

jasper: For long-term, we should move to isolated workspaces per PR or use a locking service (small DynamoDB/GCS locker or a GitHub app that grants a lease). Also consider moving state to Terraform Cloud for enforced locking if that matches governance.

sre-oncall: After the quick fixes please also add an alert on failed provision runs >3 within 1 hour to page us. Right now it's just an error in CI.

ci-bot: Related run: https://github.com/redwood/infra/actions/runs/123456789 — failing runs: 8 in last 2 hours.

maya: Patch PR opened: #456 — disables auto apply on PRs + adds note in PR checklist. Merging after quick review.

samir: I'll open #457 with concurrency + retries. ETA ~45m.

li: After those land, we should run a staged re-run on a single canary PR and watch for 409s. If still flaky, we escalate to GCP quota team.

maya: thanks all. I'll coordinate the manual re-run once both PRs are merged and post back results.

sre-oncall: Follow-up: I put a temporary 5m autoscaler cooldown on clusters to avoid immediate retries creating more API load. Keep me posted. :white_check_mark:
